text:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] 07:12 UTC — spike in TLS handshake failures originating from multiple Cloudflare EU POPs. Failure rate for /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings jumped from ~2% to ~58% over 6m. Detecting increased 525/526 and TCP handshake resets. Possible third-party/CDN issue. Paging devops-oncall.

devops-oncall: ack — I'm taking this. Putting incident channel in high priority. Investigating Cloudflare side + DNS. @ajay can you pull any origin logs and confirm if upstream certs are ok? I'll start trying quick failover steps. :phone:

ajay: seeing a lot of upstream TLS errors in nginx on eu-origin-1: 
```
[2026-03-15T07:11:56Z] "POST /v1/generate" 525 0ms "-" "cf-edge-EU-45"
[2026-03-15T07:12:02Z] "POST /v1/embeddings" 526 0ms "-" "cf-edge-EU-12"
```
Certificates on origin look fine (valid, not expired). TCP-level resets to origin from some CF edge IP ranges. Trying to pull more from tcpdump now.

marisa: support queue — we've routed ~32 tickets so far, mostly EU customers reporting immediate 5xx errors. Some customers see connection refused, others see TLS error text. Customer impact estimate: ~20% of EU traffic, higher for real-time SDKs. Drafting a status update.

devops-oncall: Datadog shows gaps for EU region (ingest delays) — Lina can you confirm observability? If Datadog is delayed we may not trust the metrics.

lina: Datadog is ingesting slowly (alerts delayed ~5-10m). Filing with Datadog support but initial is that DNS/ingest for EU was reported degraded. Also noticed Auth provider (auth0) has increased token latency but auth checks mostly succeed. So there are two third-party degradations: Cloudflare (edge/TLS) + Datadog ingest delay.

ajay: opened Cloudflare ticket #CF-9876543 (escalated to P1). Sent packet captures and sample curl reproducer. Cloudflare acknowledges widespread EU handshake anomalies and is routing to their edge team. They asked for any origin-side rate limiting logs — none on our side.

devops-oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable Cloudflare proxy (set DNS proxy off) for api.redwood.com in EU to allow direct-to-origin connections; 2) switch to secondary DNS provider for NS resolution if propagation looks slow; 3) increase origin capacity and quicken healthchecks; 4) update public status. Doing step 1 now.

devops-oncall: running Cloudflare API call to set proxied=false for the A record (reduces TLS handshake via CF):

```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/$ZONE_ID/dns_records/$RECORD_ID" \
  -H "X-Auth-Email: infra@redwood.example" \
  -H "X-Auth-Key: $CF_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"proxied":false}'
```
Posting results when it finishes.

ajay: also prepping secondary DNS change — lowering TTL to 60s before swapping A to origin IPs. If we take proxy off remember WAF+rate-limits will be bypassed; need to reapply at origin.

support-ops: prepared status draft: "We are investigating a third-party CDN issue affecting API reachability in EU. Some API requests may fail with TLS/connection errors. We're actively working with Cloudflare and will provide updates every 30 minutes." Approve? :eyes:

marisa: approve. Add note to customers using SDKs to retry idempotently and to increase client timeouts briefly.

devops-oncall: Cloudflare API call returned 200 for record update, proxied=false. Propagation in progress. Rolling TTL change now to 60s on primary DNS, then will update A records to origin IPs on both providers.

ajay: origin logs show immediate drop in 5xx after proxied=false for ~30% of requests (we're getting more direct traffic). Some CF POPs still injecting resets; Cloudflare says they're still routing and fixing.

lina: because Datadog is delayed, we've started a temporary aggregated log push to S3 via local collector so we can still run quick rollbacks/forensics. Command run on eu-origin-1: 

```bash
sudo systemctl start local-log-forwarder || true
/opt/local-forwarder/push --bucket redwood-incident-eu --since "7m ago"
```

ajay: Cloudflare just followed up: they are rolling a routing change to mitigate a buggy BPF translation in a subset of EU POPs. ETA ~15-30m. They've requested we avoid toggling proxied flag back and forth.

devops-oncall: noted. We will keep proxied=false until Cloudflare confirms fixed and we've verified stability for 10m.

support-ops: status update posted to status.redwood.ai (incident id INC-20260315-01). Sent customer email to affected orgs.

marisa: handoff note — I'm leaving in ~45m. Night oncall is @jordan. Jordan, pls take over when you ack. Key things: Cloudflare ticket P1 (#CF-9876543), proxied=false, DNS TTL lowered to 60s, S3 log push running.

jordan: Ack — I'll take over when you're offline. Uploading my contact info to the incident doc and will monitor for 2h. Plan B if we see new spikes: revert to AF_IP allowlist on ALB + temp rate limits at origin (nginx limit_req).

ajay: putting snippet to add origin allowlist (ALB security group) and nginx rate-limit example: 

```bash
# ALB SG: add CF edge IP ranges or allow direct-origin from 0.0.0.0/0 if proxied=false temporarily
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-abc123 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0

# nginx rate limit sample
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=rl:10m rate=100r/m;
server {
  location / {
    limit_req zone=rl burst=200 nodelay;
  }
}
```

sre-bot: Reminder — please fill in the incident timeline and severity fields: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/form INC-20260315-01

devops-oncall: putting final note before handoff: current state — partial recovery observed after proxied=false; Cloudflare claims mitigation rollout and monitoring. Customer impact reduced from ~20% to ~6% of EU traffic. Datadog still delayed; local log push ongoing. Support has posted communications. Next update in 20m or on major change. Jordan please confirm takeover.

jordan: confirmed takeover. Monitoring runbook in place. If Cloudflare reports completion and metrics look stable for 10m, we'll restore proxied=true and watch for regressions. If not stable, keep proxied=false and prepare long term plan with Cloudflare and DNS vendor.

incidents-bot: Incident INC-20260315-01 opened by devops-oncall at 07:12 UTC. Current severity: SEV2.

devops-oncall: thanks all — handing off to @jordan. Leaving channel but will be on call backup. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: last alert at 07:20 UTC. Please update incident when resolved or escalated further.
